questions.q: The ratio between a two-digit number and the number obtained by reversing its digits is $4:7$. Find the ratio between the tens place digit and the units place digit.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling

Dekh bhai, ye options se udane wala question hai! Pen uthane ki bhi zarurat nahi.

Pen-Free Observation: Number $ab$ aur reversed $ba$ ka ratio $4:7$ diya hai. Ratio $1$ se chota hai, matlab pehla digit dusre se chhota hoga. Option B aur D sidha eliminate ho gaye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique - Option Elimination):
Option A: Ratio $1:2$ hai. Number maano $12$. Reverse hoga $21$. Seedha $\frac{12}{21} = \frac{4}{7}$ match kar gaya. Sirf 2 second ka game tha!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Let number be $10x+y$ and reverse be $10y+x$.
$\frac{10x+y}{10y+x} = \frac{4}{7} \implies 70x + 7y = 40y + 4x \implies 66x = 33y \implies \frac{x}{y} = \frac{1}{2}$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Ratio of digits pooche toh sidha base values assume karke fraction check kar lena, equation banane mein time waste mat karna.

questions.q: A number when divided by $15$ leaves remainder $8$ and when divided by $9$ leaves remainder $a$. Which of the following regarding $a$ is TRUE?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling

Dekh bhai, isme koi fixed pattern nahi hai, SSC yaha trap set karta hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Divisor $15$ se $9$ pe jana hai. $15$ aur $9$ completely divisible nahi hain. Isliye remainder fluctuate karega. Seedha 'None' mark kar sakte ho.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique - Value Putting):
Number format: $N = 15k + 8$.
Put $k = 1 \implies N = 23$. $23 \div 9$ gives remainder $a = 5$ (Prime/Odd).
Put $k = 2 \implies N = 38$. $38 \div 9$ gives remainder $a = 2$ (Prime/Even).
Dono case me even/odd aur values badal rahi hain. Koi ek statement TRUE nahi ho sakti.

Future Exam Takeaway: Jab naya divisor purane divisor ka direct factor na ho, toh answer hamesha 'Cannot be determined' ya fluctuating aayega.

questions.q: Find the smallest value of $a$ so that $42a48b$ ($a>b$) is divisible by $11$.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Deviation & Balancing)

Dekh bhai, $11$ ki divisibility matlab odd aur even places ke sum ka deviation zero ya $11$ ka multiple karna hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Sum of odd places $= 4+a+8 = 12+a$. Sum of even places $= 2+4+b = 6+b$.
Inka difference $= (12+a) - (6+b) = 6 + a - b$. Isko $11$ ke equal rakh do (kyunki 0 nahi ho sakta as $a>b$).

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
$6 + a - b = 11 \implies a - b = 5$.
Hume smallest $a$ chahiye aur $a>b$ hai. Minimum $b$ ko $0$ rakh do. Seedha $a = 5$ aa gaya.

Future Exam Takeaway: $11$ ki divisibility ke questions me deviation equation banake values substitute karna sabse fast tarika hai.

questions.q: Find the remainder when $2^{76}$ is divided by $96$.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Base Cancellation)

Dekh bhai, jab base aur divisor coprime na ho, toh fraction ko simplify karna zaruri hota hai!

Pen-Free Observation: Divisor $96 = 2^5 \times 3$. Upar $2$ ki power hai. $2^5$ yaani $32$ seedha cancel ho jayega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Expression: $\frac{2^{76}}{2^5 \times 3}$. Upar niche $2^5$ se cut kar do. Bacha $\frac{2^{71}}{3}$.
$2 \div 3$ ka remainder $-1$ hota hai. $(-1)^{71} = -1 \implies$ Positive remainder = $3 - 1 = 2$.
Crucial Step: Jisse divide (cancel) kiya tha, end me usse wapas multiply karna padega! $2 \times 2^5 = 64$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Power based remainder me cancel karne ke baad wapas multiply karna mat bhulna, varna sidha negative marking.

questions.q: Let $k$ be a natural number and $1 \le k \le 16$. Let $A$ be a set of two-digit natural numbers which are in the form $6k+1$, $B$ be the set of two-digit prime numbers which are in the form $6k+1$. $n(A) = x, n(B) = y$, and the number of pairs of co-prime numbers of set $A$ be $z$. What is the value of $x+y+z$:
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling / Combinatorics

Dekh bhai, set aur counting ka hybrid question hai. Thoda focus se padh.

Method 1 (Concept Builder & Ninja Technique):
Condition 1: Two digit numbers format $6k+1$. Range check karo $k=2$ ($13$) se $k=16$ ($97$) tak. Total elements $x = 16 - 2 + 1 = 15$.
Condition 2: Inme prime kitne hain? Set A ke numbers hain $13, 19, 25, 31, 37, 43, 49, 55, 61, 67, 73, 79, 85, 91, 97$. Primes find kiye: $13, 19, 31, 37, 43, 61, 67, 73, 79, 97$. Total primes $y = 10$.
Condition 3: Pairs of co-primes in Set A. Total pairs $= \frac{15 \times 14}{2} = 105$. Non-coprime pairs wo honge jinke common factors honge (like 5, 7, 13). Sirf 5 ke multiples hain $25, 55, 85$ ($3$ numbers, pairs = $3$). $7$ ke multiples $49, 91$ ($1$ pair). $13$ ka multiple sirf $13, 91$ ($1$ pair). Total non-coprimes = $3+1+1 = 5$. So $z = 105 - 5 = 100$.
Final value: $x+y+z = 15 + 10 + 100 = 125$.

Future Exam Takeaway: CDS aur CGL Mains ke counting questions me hamesha ulta socho. Co-prime nikalne se better hai Total me se Non-coprime minus kar do (JSM thinking).

questions.q: $N$ is a natural number less than $1000$ and is a multiple of $5$. When $N$ is successively divided by $7$ and $8$, it leaves remainders of $2$ and $3$ respectively. How many possible values of $N$ exist?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change

Dekh bhai, successive division me seedha 'base building' equation banani hoti hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Divisors $7, 8$ ke remainders $2, 3$. Final divisor $7 \times 8 = 56$ banega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Find the least number: $8 \times 0 + 3 = 3$. Then $3 \times 7 + 2 = 23$. So general form is $N = 56k + 23$.
Hume pata hai $N$ multiple of $5$ hai. Is equation me mod $5$ lagao: $N \equiv 1k + 3 \equiv 0 \pmod 5 \implies k = 2$.
First valid number: Put $k=2 \implies 56(2) + 23 = 135$.
Next numbers will have a gap of LCM(56, 5) = $280$. So numbers are $135, 135+280=415, 695, 975$.
Total $4$ values less than $1000$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Successive division equation banake, dusri condition (multiple of 5) ke liye usko wahi mod kar diya karo, pura solve karne me time bachega.

questions.q: Let '$a$', '$b$', '$c$' be three integers which give $3, 4$ and $8$ remainders respectively when divided by $45$. What is the remainder if $3a^{2}+5b+c^{3}$ is divided by $15$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Remainder Substitution)

Dekh bhai, Arithmetic Remainder property ka ek hi usool hai - jo operation numbers ke sath bola hai, wahi remainders ke sath kar do!

Pen-Free Observation: Purana divisor $45$, naya divisor $15$. $45$ is a multiple of $15$. Toh base safe hai, a, b, c ki jagah unke purane remainders (3, 4, 8) seedhe put kar do.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Expression = $3(3)^2 + 5(4) + (8)^3 = 27 + 20 + 512 = 559$.
Ab $559$ ko $15$ se divide karna hai. $15 \times 37 = 555$. Remainder directly $4$ aayega.

Future Exam Takeaway: Check karo ki kya naya divisor purane ka factor hai? Agar hai, toh without thinking, initial remainders ko equation me daal kar solve kar do.

questions.q: The six-digit number $537xy5$ is divisible by $125$. How many such six-digit numbers are there?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Tail Limit Observation)

Dekh bhai, kisi number ki taqat uske end digits mein hoti hai. $125$ (yani $5^3$) ka divisibility rule says last $3$ digits matter karte hain.

Pen-Free Observation: Number $125$ se divisible chahiye, toh last 3 digits $xy5$ ko $125$ ka multiple hona padega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
$125$ ke multiples likho: $125, 250, 375, 500, 625, 750, 875, 1000$.
Number $xy5$ form mein hai matlab unit digit $5$ hi honi chahiye. Valid multiples dekho: $125, 375, 625, 875$.
Total $4$ aise combination banenge jahan last me $5$ aayega. Seedha tick maro aur aage badho.

Future Exam Takeaway: Divisibility of $2^n$ aur $5^n$ me hamesha only last $n$ digits check karne hote hain. Bakwas aage ke digits pe dhyan mat dena.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $7^{99}$ is divided by $344$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Negative Remainder Concept)

Dekh bhai, powers bade ho toh divisor ke aas-paas base ki power dhundhni chahiye, taaki remainder $+1$ ya $-1$ ban jaye.

Pen-Free Observation: Divisor $344$ hai. $7$ ki powers yaad kar: $7^1=7$, $7^2=49$, $7^3=343$. $343$, $344$ se bas $1$ chota hai! Boom!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
$7^{99} = (7^3)^{33} = (343)^{33}$.
Ab $343 \div 344$ ka remainder $-1$ aata hai.
$(-1)^{33} = -1$. Negative remainder allow nahi hota math me, toh isme divisor add kar do.
Real Remainder = $344 - 1 = 343$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Hamesha power ko aise split karo ki base, divisor ke $\pm 1$ range mein aa jaye. Arithmetic ki cycle bohot fast chalti hai is format pe.

questions.q: What is the least number must be subtracted from $56785$ so that the given number become perfect Square?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Approximation & Range Definition

Dekh bhai, yaha long division method lagane wala fail hoga. Smart observation se seconds me udana hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Base square dhundho. $200^2 = 40000$, $250^2 = 62500$. $56785$ inke beech mein hai. $240^2 = 57600$. Yeh $57600$ se thoda hi chhota hai. Try $238^2$.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique - Unit Digit Trap):
$238^2 = (240-2)^2 = 57600 - 960 + 4 = 56644$.
Perfect square jo range me hai wo $56644$ hai. Difference nikal le: $56785 - 56644 = 141$. Seedha $141$ subtract karna padega.

Future Exam Takeaway: Squares ke around calculation mental math se estimate karke seedha hit karo. Base $50$ ya $100$ ka shortcut har jagah lagta hai.

questions.q: What is the sum of all integer values of $n$ for which $n^2 + 19n + 92$ is a perfect square?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling / Quadratic Completion

Dekh bhai, jab polynomial perfect square banani ho toh 'completing the square' lagana padta hai, bina pen ruke.

Method 1 (Concept Builder to Ninja Shortcut):
Let $n^2 + 19n + 92 = k^2$. Multiply whole equation by $4$ (to remove fractions).
$4n^2 + 76n + 368 = 4k^2$. Isko complete karo: $(2n+19)^2 - 361 + 368 = 4k^2$.
$(2n+19)^2 - 4k^2 = -7 \implies (2n+19-2k)(2n+19+2k) = -7$.
Since $-7$ prime hai, factors sirf $(\pm 1, \mp 7)$ honge. Symmetric roots aate hain in cases me. Sum of all integer values unke midpoint ke double pe settle hoti hai. Solving gives roots $n = -8, -11$. Sum is $-19$.

Ninja Hack: Aise format $n^2 + bn + c$ me sum of valid integer values humesha $-b$ ke barabar hota hai agar discriminant allow kare! Yaha $b=19$, toh sum seedha $-19$ aayega. Pen chhod de!

Future Exam Takeaway: 'Sum of all integers for a quadratic perfect square' puche toh $-b$ ka mental hack yaad rakhna, exam me $1$ minute save karega.

questions.q: A number $N$ leaves a remainder of $4$ when divided by $7$. What will be the remainder when the expression $(N^3 + 3N^2 + 5N + 1)$ is divided by $7$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Polynomial Substitution)

Dekh bhai, Polynomial remainder theory ka yahi fayda hai, actual number ki koi value nahi hoti, sirf uska chhota remainder matter karta hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Divisor $7$ same hai, aur $N \equiv 4 \pmod 7$. Jaha $N$ hai waha seedha $4$ daal do.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Substitute $N = 4$ in $(N^3 + 3N^2 + 5N + 1)$.
$= 4^3 + 3(4^2) + 5(4) + 1 = 64 + 48 + 20 + 1 = 133$.
Now divide $133$ by $7$. $133 = 7 \times 19$. Exact multiple hai! Toh remainder kya bacha? Seedha $0$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Algebraic expressions modulo mein behave bilkul normal addition/multiplication jaise karte hain. Remainder nikal kar seedha expression me ghusa do.

questions.q: When $999999\dots$ ($104$ times) is divided by $271$, the remainder that remains is:
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change (Repdigit Cyclicity)

Dekh bhai, prime numbers ki repeating digits me cyclic property (magic multiples) hoti hai. $271$ ka relation $9$ series me kahan banta hai, ye pata hona chahiye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Tujhe pata hona chahiye $271 \times 369 = 99999$ (5 baar 9). Matlab har $5$ baar $9$ ka block $271$ se completely divide hoke $0$ remainder dega.
Total digits hain $104$. Isko $5$ ke blocks me tod do: $104 \div 5$, bacha $4$ digits.
Pehle $100$ digits consume ho gaye. End me sirf $4$ digits bache: $9999$.
Ab bs $9999 \div 271$ karna hai. $271 \times 36 = 9756$.
$9999 - 9756 = 243$. Answer aa gaya!

Future Exam Takeaway: Magic numbers yaad kar le: $1001 = 7 \times 11 \times 13$, aur $99999 = 271 \times 369 \times 1$. Cyclicity ka length digit grouping me kaam aata hai.

questions.q: Find the sum of the reciprocals of all the factors of $360$.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Reciprocal Symmetry)

Dekh bhai, yahan sab factors likh kar fraction add karega toh agla attempt dena padega. Direct trick lagani hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique Formula):
Sum of Reciprocals of Factors = $\frac{\text{Sum of Factors}}{N}$.
Pehle $360$ ka prime factorization kar: $360 = 2^3 \times 3^2 \times 5^1$.
Sum of factors formula: $\frac{2^4-1}{2-1} \times \frac{3^3-1}{3-1} \times \frac{5^2-1}{5-1}$
$= 15 \times 13 \times 6 = 1170$.
Ab seedha value daal: $\frac{1170}{360} = \frac{117}{36} = \frac{13}{4} = 3.25$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Sum of reciprocals ka ek universal shortcut $\frac{\text{Sum of Divisors}}{N}$ apni notes me bold karke likh lo.

questions.q: The sum of a two-digit number and the number obtained by reversing its digits is a perfect square. How many such two-digit numbers are there?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Digital Balancing)

Dekh bhai, reversing digits hamesha basic algebraic form me tut-te hain. Wahi se constraint balancing karni hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Number $10x+y$ and reverse $10y+x$. Inka sum hamesha $11(x+y)$ hota hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Sum $= 11(x+y)$. Perfect square banane ke liye isme ek aur $11$ chahiye, yani $(x+y)$ ko $11$ banna hi padega (ya 44 ban sakta hai but digits ka sum 18 se bada nahi hota).
So, $x+y = 11$.
Valid digit pairs: $(2,9), (3,8), (4,7), (5,6)$.
Inke reversed pairs bhi honge: $(9,2), (8,3), (7,4), (6,5)$.
Total numbers $4 + 4 = 8$ ho gaye. Seedha count karo.

Future Exam Takeaway: Sum of reversed two-digit numbers always multiple of $11$, and difference is always multiple of $9$. Ye static facts seconds bachate hain.

questions.q: The product of three consecutive positive integers is always exactly divisible by which of the following numbers?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Factorial Property)

Dekh bhai, ye CDS ka standard theoretical trap hai. Ise bina values rakhe theory se udana hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Rule hai ki koi bhi $n$ lagatar integers ka product hamesha $n!$ se divide hoga.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Yaha $3$ consecutive positive integers diye hain. Us particular rule se seedha $3!$ ka factor lagega.
$3! = 3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6$. So, product $6$ se humesha exact divisible hoga. Dummy check: $1 \times 2 \times 3 = 6$ (divisible by 6).

Future Exam Takeaway: Agar $n$ consecutive numbers ka question aaye, toh bina soche usme $n!$ ka divisibility rule laga dena. Time save hoga.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $(10^{10} + 10^{100} + 10^{1000} + 10^{10000})$ is divided by $7$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change (Fermat's Cyclic Pattern)

Dekh bhai, base agar bada ho aur divisor prime ho, toh seedha Fermat's theorem lagake powers choti karni hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Base $10 \equiv 3 \pmod 7$. Toh $(3^{10} + 3^{100} + 3^{1000} + 3^{10000}) \pmod 7$. Fermat's says cyclicity is $7-1 = 6$. Powers ko 6 se divide karke chota kar lo.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Powers hain $10, 100, 1000...$
$10 \div 6 \implies$ Remainder $4$.
$100 \div 6 \implies$ Remainder $4$.
Dhyan se dekh, 10 ki har power ko $6$ se divide karne pe $4$ hi remainder aayega.
Toh expression bana: $3^4 + 3^4 + 3^4 + 3^4$.
$3^4 = 81 \equiv 4 \pmod 7$.
So char baar $4$ aayega. Sum = $4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 16$.
$16 \pmod 7 = 2$. Seedha answer!

Future Exam Takeaway: Modulo prime wale questions me Fermat's chhota base-power banata hai. Powers ko divisor ki cyclicity ($P-1$) se pehle hi kaat do.

questions.q: If the 10-digit number $5432y1749x$ is divisible by $72$, what is the minimum possible value of $(5x - 4y)$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Base Divisibility Balancing)

Dekh bhai, $72$ ka direct divisibility rule nahi hota, humesha isko co-primes $8$ aur $9$ mein todna hota hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Step 1: Rule of $8$ for last 3 digits. $49x$ must be divisible by $8$. $8 \times 60 = 480$, agla multiple $488$, fir $496$. Toh seedha $x = 6$ locked.
Step 2: Rule of $9$ for sum of digits. Sum = $5+4+3+2+y+1+7+4+9+6 = 41 + y$.
Sum must be multiple of $9$. $41$ ke baad $45$ aata hai. So $41 + y = 45 \implies y = 4$.
Dono variables mil gaye. Final calculation: $5(6) - 4(4) = 30 - 16 = 14$.

Future Exam Takeaway: $72, 88, 99$ jaise bade divisors me JSM ki tarah do alag divisibility parts ko balance karte hain. Humesha end digits (jaise 8) se start karo, fir sum of digits (jaise 9 ya 11) par aao.

questions.q: A number when divided by $4$ and $5$ successively leaves remainders of $1$ and $4$ respectively. What will be the successive remainders when the same number is divided by $5$ and $4$ successively?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change (Base Formation)

Dekh bhai, successive division me least valid number bottom-up approach se nikala jata hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Divisors $(4, 5)$ and Remainders $(1, 4)$.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Number formation (Bottom-up): Least value ke liye last quotient $0$ maan lo.
Step 1: $5 \times 0 + 4 = 4$
Step 2: $4 \times 4 + 1 = 17$
Number nikal gaya $17$.
Ab pucha hai reverse successive division by $5, 4$.
Step A: $17 \div 5 \implies$ Quotient $3$, Remainder $2$.
Step B: Quotient $3 \div 4 \implies$ Quotient $0$, Remainder $3$.
Final remainders $2$ and $3$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Successive division hamesha last step se upar chalti hai. Base calculation ke bad normal division cascade laga diya karo.

questions.q: Calculate the sum: $1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + \dots + 21 = ?$
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM / AP Average Shift

Dekh bhai, Arithmetic Progression lagaoge toh time jayega, seedha odd numbers ka static rule lagao.

Pen-Free Observation: Sequence starting se $1, 3, 5...$ odd numbers ka hai. First $n$ odd numbers ka sum humesha $n^2$ hota hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Last term $21$ hai. $n$-th odd term ka formula hota hai $(2n - 1)$.
$(2n - 1) = 21 \implies 2n = 22 \implies n = 11$.
Sum $= n^2 = 11^2 = 121$. Khatam.

Future Exam Takeaway: Odd number sums par standard AP methods waste of time hain. Seedha $n$ nikalo aur $n^2$ thoko.

questions.q: When two numbers are separately divided by $44$ the remainders are $11$ and $38$ respectively. If the sum of the two number is divided by $44$, then the obtained remainder will be?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Remainder Addition)

Dekh bhai, remainder theorem ka universal law hai: Jo numbers ka operation bola hai, wahi unke remainders ka kardo.

Pen-Free Observation: Dono case mein divisor $44$ hai. Final divisor bhi $44$ hai. Seedha remainders add kar do.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Naye number ka base banega $11 + 38 = 49$.
Ab directly $49$ ko $44$ se divide kar de. $49 \pmod{44}$ seedha remainder $5$ dega. Pen rakh do!

Future Exam Takeaway: Add, Subtract ya multiply, jo operation numbers ke saath likha ho woh hamesha base remainders par utar diya karo. Constants maintain rehte hain.

questions.q: Value of $22.\overline{4} + 11.5\overline{67} - 33.5\overline{9}$ is?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Bar Decimals Shift)

Dekh bhai, Bar (recurring) decimals ko fraction me break karne se time waste hoga. Direct column wise add karke approximate karo.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Expand the values vertically till 4 decimal places:
$22.4444...$
$+ 11.5676...$
$------------- $
$34.0120...$
Now, subtract the third value ($33.5999...$, which is practically $33.6000$):
$34.0120 - 33.6000 = 0.4120$
Pattern matching: The outcome stabilizes around $0.41212...$ i.e., $0.4\overline{12}$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Recurring decimals ki equation fractions se handle karne ke bajaye, unhe $3-4$ digit tak open kar lo, aur column approach se seedha answer dikh jayega.

questions.q: The expression $333^{555} + 555^{333}$ is divisible by
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Cross-Product / Modulo Factorization

Dekh bhai, expression ke base bhot suspicious hain. Yahan prime factorization aur parity rule check karni hoti hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Rule 1 (Divisibility by 2): $333^{555}$ = $Odd^{Odd}$ = Odd. $555^{333}$ = $Odd^{Odd}$ = Odd. Odd + Odd = Even. Toh divisible by $2$ hai.
Rule 2 (Divisibility by 3 & 37): Note kar $111$ ke dono multiples hain. $333 = 3 \times 111$ and $555 = 5 \times 111$. Aur $111 = 3 \times 37$. Matlab $333$ aur $555$ dono $3$ aur $37$ ke multiples hain. Jab base me hi factors baithe hain, toh poora expression dono se completely divisible hoga.
Since $2, 3$ aur $37$ teeno satisfies ho gaye, seedha 'All of these' maro.

Future Exam Takeaway: $111$ aur uske multiples ($222, 333$ etc.) $37 \times 3$ format mein break hote hain. SSC in bases par baar baar question frame karta hai.

questions.q: What is the sum of all $3$ digit positive integers divisible by $11$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM / AP Average Scaling

Dekh bhai, Arithmetic Progression ke sum ko hum average method se jaldi approach karenge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
First 3-digit number divisible by $11 = 110$. Last number $= 990$.
Number of terms $n = \frac{\text{Last} - \text{First}}{\text{Common Difference}} + 1 = \frac{990 - 110}{11} + 1 = \frac{880}{11} + 1 = 81$.
Sum is basically (Number of terms) $\times$ (Average of sequence).
Average $= \frac{110 + 990}{2} = 550$.
Sum $= 81 \times 550 = 44550$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Sum of AP hamesha $n \times \text{Middle term (ya average)}$ se speed me nikala karo, $\frac{n}{2}[2a+(n-1)d]$ baccho wale formula par reliance kam karo.

questions.q: What is the sum of all the common terms less than $632$ between the given series $S_1$ and $S_2$. $S_1 = 2, 9, 16, 23 \dots, 632$ and $S_2 = 7, 11, 15, \dots, 743$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM / LCM Sequence Builder

Dekh bhai, 2 parallel series ka common sequence directly LCM of differences se nikalta hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
$S_1$ ka difference $= 7$. $S_2$ ka difference $= 4$.
Common series ka difference $D = LCM(7, 4) = 28$.
Dono me pehla common term manually observe kar. $S_1$ is $2, 9, 16, 23$. $S_2$ is $7, 11, 15, 19, 23$. First common term $a = 23$.
Common series bani: $23, 51, 79 \dots$ less than $632$.
Max terms: $23 + (n-1)28 < 632 \implies (n-1)28 < 609 \implies n-1 \le 21.75$. Toh $n = 22$.
Last term $l = 23 + 21 \times 28 = 611$.
Sum $= \frac{n}{2}(a+l) = 11 \times (23 + 611) = 11 \times 634 = 6974$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Jab do APs merge karni ho toh first matching term manual dhundho aur naya difference seedha dono old differences ka LCM utha lo.
